findings.title: Changed a frontend interpolation key to Java MessageFormat syntax
findings.body: This account UI message bundle uses i18next-style placeholders such as `{{0}}`, `{{name}}`, and React component placeholders such as `<0>`. Replacing `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}` with `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2}` means the account UI will no longer interpolate the attribute name or bounds and will display those braces literally. The Java `choice` expression is also not a pluralization format understood by this frontend message format.

findings.title: Changed an admin UI translation from its supported placeholder syntax
findings.body: The admin UI message resources use `{{0}}`-style frontend interpolation. This change switches the message to Java MessageFormat placeholders and a `choice` expression, so the admin UI will render `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2,...}` as literal text rather than substituting the validation values. Keep this bundle in the frontend translation format and handle pluralization using the UI i18n mechanism if needed.

findings.title: Lithuanian TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `messages_lt.properties` is the Lithuanian account-theme bundle, but the new `totpStep1` value is Italian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`). Lithuanian users will see an unrelated-language instruction during authenticator setup.

findings.title: Lithuanian login TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian login-theme bundle now contains the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare` for `loginTotpStep1`. This is user-visible on the Lithuanian login flow and should be replaced with a Lithuanian translation.
